text.p: Dutch-Belgian financial group Fortis on Thursday beat analysts' expectations with an 18 percent rise in nine month net profits to 554 million Ecus ($696.7 million) and raised full year expectations.

"We are very happy. We are raising our forecasts. For Fortis we now expect a rise (in 1996) of 12 to 15 percent," said Fortis co-chairman Maurice Lippens in a Reuters Financial Television (RFTV) interview.
Fortis said earlier this year it expected profit was likely to increase by at least 10 percent over 1995's 631 million Ecus.
Analysts, who on average had expected the group to report a nine month profit of around 549 million Ecus, were upbeat on the results and new forecast.
"The general impression is positive. Good figures," said analyst Jacob Bosscha of Bank Labouchere.
"My full-year forecast might go up a few cents (per share) but it won't be a drastic revision," he added.

Dutch Fortis Amev, which merged with Belgian AG in 1989 to form Fortis, posted a net profit of 605 million guilders ($351.7 million) versus 519 million guilders in the same period of 1995. Earnings per share (EPS) rose 15 percent to 3.33 guilders.
Fortis AG profits rose by 21 percent to 10.052 billion Belgian francs, with EPS up 15 percent to 266 francs.

"For the parent companies, Fortis AMEV quoted in Amsterdam and Fortis AG in Brussels, whereas before we expected growth in earnings per share of between 7 and 12 percent, we are raising this to a minimum 10 percent," Lippens said.

He said the profit rise was mainly due to a much stronger than expected performance of Fortis' life insurance businesses. Ordinary premium income was a little higher in the Netherlands and flat in Belgium.
Lippens said Fortis in the Netherlands made "quite a large provision" in one part of its accident and health business, but this was a one-time charge and not structural.
A provision for restructuring foreign exchange operations pushed the operating banking result in the Netherlands eight percent lower than the same period last year at 67 million Ecu.
But in Belgium the operating result for banking showed an increase of 25 percent to 332 million Ecus compared to the same period of 1995.
"Banking was slightly better than expected," said analyst Dick Erdman of Gilissen Bankiers.

Analyst Ton Gietman of Van Meer James Capel said Fortis had said at the interims it expected banking to show clearly lower profits in the second half. "But this did not happen in the third quarter," Gietman said.
Lippens said Fortis' U.S. accident and health operations, which had been a drag on profit in recent quarters, had started turning a positive result. "We are not in the red anymore," he said.

Shares in both parent companies rose on the news. Fortis Amev, slightly up before the nine months figures were released, rose further in early afternoon to 56.90 guilders, up 1.80 guilders. One analyst said he had the shares at a strong buy, saying in the short-term the shares could rise to 65 guilders.
Fortis AG shares traded up 80 Belgian francs to 4890. ($ = 0.795 European Currency Unit -- Ecus) ($ = 1.720 Dutch Guilders)
